items.title: Consulting the timetable
items.desc: Students consult their approved weekly timetable and the announcements addressed to them. Only timetables published for the groups in which they are enrolled are visible.

items.title: Preparing the lesson
items.desc: The instructor uploads the lecture material and receives a structured lesson with vocabulary and review questions which is then reviewed and revised before publication.

items.title: Conducting the examination
items.desc: Examination time is measured on the server and grading takes place there. Proctoring runs on the student's device and no image is sent away for analysis.

items.title: Recording attendance
items.desc: Lecture attendance is recorded electronically alongside an indicator of each student's participation in activities and assignments.

items.title: Individual follow up
items.desc: A remedial assignment is issued to one specific student to address identified weaknesses with instructions and attachments intended for that student alone.

items.title: The analytical report
items.desc: Each course presents its strengths and weaknesses and recommendations for improvement derived from progress and participation and attendance data.

capabilities.title: An integrated system rather than separate tools
capabilities.desc: The following components operate together within a single environment. They may be browsed by area.

cards.title: AI assisted content preparation
cards.desc: Converting PDF and Word files and scanned pages into lessons and examinations that remain open to review and revision before publication.

cards.title: Multilevel courses
cards.desc: Courses organised into levels and units comprising lessons and video material and short quizzes and assignments with student progress saved automatically.

cards.title: Individual remedial assignments
cards.desc: An assignment issued to a single student to address specific weaknesses with dedicated instructions and attachments.

cards.title: Examinations and homework
cards.desc: Timing set by the server and grading performed there. Correct answers never reach the student's device at any stage.

cards.title: Proctoring on the student's device
cards.desc: Detection of the face and gaze direction and phones and books and the presence of another person within the student's own browser.

cards.title: Live proctoring
cards.desc: Audio and video of every student during the examination with an immediate indication of who is speaking.

cards.title: Appeals against flags
cards.desc: A guaranteed right for the student to appeal any recorded flag with the decision made by the instructor.

cards.title: Attendance and participation
cards.desc: Recording of lecture attendance with a participation indicator for each student derived from actual activity.

cards.title: Weekly timetables
cards.desc: An approved timetable for every group published to students and a private timetable for each instructor.

cards.title: Record retention and recovery
cards.desc: Data is never permanently erased. It is moved to an institutional archive that allows recovery and preserves the academic record across years.

cards.title: Administrative reports
cards.desc: Reports exportable to Excel that present statistical indicators without disclosing examination content.

cards.title: Institutional announcements
cards.desc: Announcements designed within the browser and directed to specific groups of students.

cards.title: Administrative correspondence
cards.desc: A unified channel through which instructors submit requests to the administration and follow them until resolution.

cards.title: Institutional mail
cards.desc: Linking the institution's Gmail account to correspond with students and instructors from within the platform.

privacy.title: Proctoring that preserves student privacy
privacy.desc: Video is analysed within the student's browser and no frame is sent to a server for analysis. Compare what takes place on the student's device with what reaches the instructor.
device: Analysis of facial features and gaze direction.
Detection of phones and books and the presence of another person.
Recording of leaving the examination page or exiting full screen.
Recording of ambient sound during the examination.
privacy.deviceNote: If a detector cannot be started this is recorded as a technical note and is not treated as a violation.
privacy.teacherNote: The instructor receives an event log and small snapshots of serious violations only. No one else can see them and they are permanently deleted after 30 hours.

fairness.title: No violation is upheld before the student is heard
fairness.desc: Every recorded flag follows a clear procedure that guarantees the student's right of appeal. The final decision rests with the instructor and not with an algorithm.

steps.title: Detection
steps.desc: Proctoring records the event with its time and type and severity.

steps.title: Appeal
steps.desc: The student submits a reasoned appeal from the results page.

steps.title: Review
steps.desc: The instructor reviews the event and the appeal and issues a decision.

steps.title: Documentation
steps.desc: The appeal and its outcome are entered in the administration report.

centre.title: Defined permissions for the continuing education centre

insights.title: Analysis that informs academic decisions

insights.weakness: Completion of unit four is lower than in the other units.

insights.ai: It is recommended that a short formative quiz covering the core concepts of unit four be introduced midway through the unit. Students who have not completed it should be followed up through individual remedial assignments whose results are reviewed the following week.

hero.title: Security and privacy at the heart of the platform
hero.desc: This page explains the technical safeguards that protect assessment integrity and the confidentiality of institutional and student data. These safeguards are enforced on the server and in the database and not in the interface alone.

explorer.title: Select a risk to see the safeguard that addresses it

threats.title: Forging grades
threats.safeguard: Grades are computed on the server from the model answers stored there. User accounts have no direct write access to result tables.

threats.title: Extending examination time
threats.safeguard: The start time of an examination is recorded on the server when it begins. Refreshing the page or changing the device clock does not change the remaining time.

threats.title: Viewing another institution's data
threats.safeguard: Every read and write in the database is restricted to the user's own institution. Access attempts between institutions have been tested to confirm that they fail.

threats.title: Granting oneself permissions
threats.safeguard: Role and permission columns are pinned in the database so users cannot change their own. Permissions are verified on the server before every sensitive operation.

threats.title: Joining without authorisation
threats.safeguard: Accounts are created only with a valid invitation from the institution. Google is used for signing in only and never for creating accounts.

threats.title: Leaking student images
threats.safeguard: The camera stream is analysed inside the student's browser. Only small snapshots are sent for serious violations and only the exam teacher sees them through temporary links before they are permanently deleted after 30 hours.

threats.title: Accidental deletion
threats.safeguard: Data is never permanently erased. It moves to an institutional archive from which it can be recovered.

threats.title: Overuse of services
threats.safeguard: Rate limits apply to costly operations for each user separately.

items.title: User browser
items.desc: The camera is analysed locally and model answers never reach the browser at any stage.

items.title: Access gate
items.desc: Every page verifies the user's identity and account status and role before it is shown.

items.title: Server services
items.desc: Sensitive operations run only after checking permissions and confirming that the data belongs to the user's institution.

map.desc: Browse the tasks of the platform to see which of them use artificial intelligence and which do not.

tasks.title: Lesson from a title
tasks.desc: A proposed lesson is generated from a title chosen by the instructor who then reviews it before publishing.

tasks.title: Lesson from a file
tasks.desc: Lecture material including scanned pages is read and a structured lesson is built from it.

tasks.title: Examinations and homework
tasks.desc: Questions of varied types are proposed with model answers and the instructor selects and edits them.

tasks.title: Course from a presentation
tasks.desc: A presentation is turned into a course of editable units and lessons.

tasks.title: Individual assignment draft
tasks.desc: On request a draft remedial assignment is proposed for one student based on their weaknesses.

tasks.title: Announcement wording
tasks.desc: On request a title and body are suggested for an announcement.

tasks.title: Elaborating recommendations
tasks.desc: Recommendations are derived from fixed rules and their wording is elaborated with AI only on request.

tasks.title: Examination proctoring
tasks.desc: Face and object detection models run inside the student's browser and no image is sent to an external provider.

tasks.title: Grading answers
tasks.desc: Objective questions are graded on the server against model answers and instructors grade essay answers.

tasks.title: Deciding on flags
tasks.desc: The instructor decides every appeal after reviewing the event.

tasks.title: Course analysis
tasks.desc: Strengths and weaknesses are derived by fixed published rules from progress and participation and attendance data.

flow.title: No generated content reaches students without review

steps.title: Source material
steps.desc: The instructor uploads a file or chooses a lesson title.

steps.title: Text extraction
steps.desc: Files are read including scanned pages.

steps.title: Draft preparation
steps.desc: A proposed lesson or examination is generated to a defined structure.

steps.title: Human review
steps.desc: The instructor reviews the draft and edits or rejects it.

steps.title: Release to students
steps.desc: Content is published only by the instructor's decision.

principles.title: Rules that govern the use of artificial intelligence

items.title: Review before release
items.desc: Everything AI generates is a draft until the instructor approves it.

items.title: On request never automatic
items.desc: AI services are not called when pages open but only when a user explicitly asks.

items.title: Fair usage limits
items.desc: Each user has an hourly ceiling on requests to keep the service stable.

items.title: Protecting student images
items.desc: Student images and camera streams are never sent to any AI provider.

items.title: Published rules first
items.desc: Analyses rest on fixed explainable rules and AI is used for wording only.

never.title: What artificial intelligence does not do on the platform
items: It does not grade student answers.
It does not decide on flags or appeals.
It does not see camera streams during examinations.
It does not publish content without the instructor's decision.

cta.title: Try content preparation yourself
cta.desc: Explore the demonstration or request an introductory presentation in which we show the full cycle of preparing and reviewing content.
